chapters.title: Sort Out the Three Conversations
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter is a diagnostic entry point: every difficult exchange contains the what-happened, feelings, and identity conversations, with identity often least visible and most powerful.
chapters.coreMove: Separate a recent hard exchange into its facts, feelings, and identity layers before choosing any response.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating the three conversations as a tidy checklist or as the solution itself.

chapters.title: Stop Arguing About Who's Right
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter replaces message delivery with the learning stance and stresses that performed openness is not the same as genuine curiosity.
chapters.coreMove: Hold your story as one coherent version and ask what the other person sees that your position cannot see.
chapters.commonMisread: Being nicer while still trying to deliver a verdict.

chapters.title: Don't Assume They Meant It
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter disentangles intent and impact, especially the deliverer-side failure of using good intent to dismiss harm.
chapters.coreMove: Acknowledge the impact as real before explaining what you meant.
chapters.commonMisread: Assuming good intentions are enough or treating hurt feelings as proof of malice.

chapters.title: Abandon Blame
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter trades blame for contribution while preserving asymmetry and accountability limits.
chapters.coreMove: Map the repeating contribution system and identify one move of yours that keeps it alive.
chapters.commonMisread: False parity, self-blame, or using contribution language to excuse the person with more power.

chapters.title: Have Your Feelings (Or They Will Have You)
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter says feelings are already in the room and teaches how to name them accurately without turning them into accusations.
chapters.coreMove: Translate a vague or disguised feeling into a direct report you can own.
chapters.commonMisread: Dumping emotion or suppressing it in the name of professionalism.

chapters.title: Ground Your Identity
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter shows how all-or-nothing identity beliefs create identity quakes and how AND/BOTH grounding prepares the self-image to receive hard information.
chapters.coreMove: Ground the threatened identity belief before the conversation by making it complex enough to hold bad news.
chapters.commonMisread: Using AND/BOTH as self-soothing language that prevents feedback from leaving a mark.

chapters.title: What's Your Purpose? When to Raise It, When to Let Go
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter asks whether to raise the conversation at all by sorting legitimate purposes from warning-sign purposes and distinguishing letting go from suppression.
chapters.coreMove: Choose a conversation only when its honest purpose is something that conversation can actually produce.
chapters.commonMisread: Raising every grievance because honesty sounds virtuous.

chapters.title: Begin from the Third Story
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter has one main move: replace first-story openers with a third-story opener plus genuine invitation.
chapters.coreMove: Start from a neutral description of the gap between views and invite comparison rather than defense.
chapters.commonMisread: Softening an accusation while leaving your story as the baseline.

chapters.title: Listen from the Inside Out
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter locates listening inside the listener: notice counterargument, judgment, and identity management before using questions, paraphrase, and acknowledgment.
chapters.coreMove: Set down the internal voice long enough for the other person's meaning to arrive.
chapters.commonMisread: Equating listening with silence, eye contact, or scripted paraphrase.

chapters.title: Speak for Yourself with Clarity and Power
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter teaches owned expression: observation, internal response, and the story you began telling, plus honesty calibration under reaction.
chapters.coreMove: Report your experience as discussable material without turning your interpretation into a verdict.
chapters.commonMisread: Generic assertiveness or softer accusations labeled as I-statements.

chapters.title: Problem-Solving: Take the Lead
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter shifts into design only when ready, avoiding drift and unilateral prescription through joint inquiry, options, standards, and specific agency-matched commitments.
chapters.coreMove: Lead the process of solving together without taking ownership of the solution away from the other person.
chapters.commonMisread: Jumping to fix the issue before understanding and expression have happened.

chapters.title: Putting It All Together
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter integrates the whole arc and warns that the framework is not a script; openness to being changed is the real skill, with real limits around non-engagement, power gaps, old issues, and written media.
chapters.coreMove: Compose the right move for the live situation while staying genuinely open to what may change.
chapters.commonMisread: Recapping a checklist or performing the framework mechanically.
